payload.text: D-ADR0055: Event truth is sealed changesets as git objects on per-machine refs -- an event is acknowledged when fsynced in the store's open log outside the work tree and becomes git truth when sealed by compare-and-swap into a commit on refs/fgos/events/<machine-id>; machines share by pushing the own ref and fetching the others; every view is a rebuildable cache. Supersedes L3 clauses 1 and 4 (ae461c8b) and the data layout of D-ADR0003 (tracked events.jsonl, gitignored state.json); L3 clauses 2 and 3 stand. Owner confirmations: machine id owned by Event Store until a machine-identity component exists; non-git directories refused; porting store writes its own project-scope stream; eventStore.sync.intervalSec 300 with opportunistic push; compaction opened when a full rebuild exceeds 2 s on the slowest machine.
payload.rationale: The event log living in the git work tree caused most git and lock incidents (investigation-261017-1027, git lessons catalogue); spec docs/platform/event-store/spec.md passed council 2, the reopened council, a model check run twice and the V-REF-01 git experiment. Review threshold: a cross-machine conflict resolved by hand more than once a month, or any acknowledged event lost while fgOS was running.
payload.alternatives: M1 hot shards in work tree (council 1 rejected), SQLite WAL as truth (out of scope), central coordinator (impossible offline on three machines)
payload.source: owner (van.tran), 2026-10-17

payload.text: D-ADR0057: Git is one foundation component (fgos-git, Rust live core) that owns every git mutation and its recovery -- typed operations (Inspect, Refs, Worktree, ScopedCommit, Sync, Land, SafeRestore, RepositoryConfig, Remote, Recovery, Publication), no public git(args) door, a hash-chained file WAL under the git common dir as the sole recovery authority, one target attempt per operation, 4.3-R locks reused (20 -> 40 -> 50, branch refs under worktree-admin 40), Node reaching Rust through one combined N-API addon shared with fgos-event-store, and the refs/fgos/* Publication port that Event Store calls; the three parallel git cores are deleted in the same release that switches their callers.
payload.rationale: Three parallel git cores and the event log in the work tree caused most git and lock incidents (git lessons catalogue, 234 entries); the owner wants one authority done once. Architecture council wf-run-1792246479016-19b58eab, owner answers 2026-10-17 23:18, proofs and two re-checks 2026-10-18 (docs/platform/git/spec.md section 19).
payload.alternatives: Node core with Rust later (10-16 council panelist 2, rejected by owner Q6); host-process route per operation (rejected Q1, spawn cost); repository-as-WAL (rejected Q3); separate Event Store and Git addons (rejected Q1, no shared load).
payload.source: owner (van.tran), 2026-10-18 09:13 ('ký nhé')
